Carry placed in its own history by REPORTED RANK, not by a distribution held: ~US$550/t intraday on ~2026-08-24 was 'highest in more than five years' (~99th pct of 5y) and US$434/t 'highest since October 2021'; it fell to ~US$175-248/t within two to three sessions, a 55-68% collapse, from US$45/t about two weeks earlier. Direction: sharply flattening. No z-score is emitted because no spread history is held (copper.lme-cash-three-month-curve UNAVAILABLE). Attribution (4a): the spread halved while the outright LME 3M price ROSE +0.4% to a record -> 0% of the outright move explained by the carry collapse; they moved in opposite directions. This is the configuration in which a spot win and a total-return loss coexist.

Explicit gap row, emitted so the absence is machine-visible. A true physical basis = nearest lawful physical/spot assessment MINUS the deliverable futures price, after aligning grade, warehouse eligibility, location, delivery date, currency and unit. No such aligned assessment is reachable in this environment; restricted benchmark data remains manual/unavailable and no licence was worked around. Zero strength, neutral, non-voting. The LME cash-3M near-dated basis is emitted once under curve-carry and is deliberately not repeated here.

COMEX front (2026-08-25 close 6.7125/lb = US$14,798/t) minus LME 3M (2026-08-26, US$14,251/t) = +US$547/t (+3.8%); using COMEX Dec-26 6.7270/lb = US$14,830/t gives +US$579/t (+4.1%). Reported at 'levels not seen since last autumn'. ALIGNMENT CAVEATS, without which this is not an arb: COMEX Grade 1 vs LME Grade A are different brand/eligibility lists; COMEX is US-warehouse-linked vs LME's global network; COMEX front vs an LME rolling 3-month prompt is a ~2-month date mismatch; freight, duty and VAT are NOT deducted, so this is a GROSS venue spread that overstates the net arbitrage. Currency is USD on both legs; unit converted at 2,204.62 lb/t. SHFE (RMB/t, VAT and bonded regime) is not additive and was not converted. Required series copper.regional-arbitrage is UNAVAILABLE.

Yangshan / China import premium on an LME basis, CIF Shanghai, USD/t: EQ copper late-Aug arrival ~US$75/t, Sept arrival US$75-85/t, registered B/L Aug arrival US$110-120/t (August 2026). Placement: below its own recent range, reported to have peaked last year and traded materially lower since; direction weakening, with the SHFE/LME price ratio deteriorating. Vendor assessment (SMM), unvintaged and unverified. This is a regional premium, NOT a China demand verdict - China activity is a demand input owned by commodity-macro-drivers and is not proof of copper demand without a primary end-use or refined-balance series.

Delivery-pressure evidence only (warrant mechanics, load-out intent), NOT an inventory vote: accessible inventory is causally owned by commodity-demand-inventory (copper.visible-inventory and copper.inventory-accessibility-opacity, both UNAVAILABLE) and is cross-referenced, not re-emitted. Evidence: roughly half of remaining LME stock earmarked for withdrawal at the peak of the squeeze; 51,400 t of withdrawal orders on 2026-08-24; 65,400 t earmarked over recent days; 42-session stock decline reported as the longest since 2014. No emergency exchange rule or EFP dislocation was reported, and absence of a report is not proof of absence. Assessed verdict: STRESSED through 2026-08-24; formal status NOT ASSESSABLE for conviction because every input is unvintaged secondary reporting.

The opposing fact, emitted separately rather than netted against the squeeze row: more than 20,000 t delivered into LME warehouses on 2026-08-25 (largest one-day on-warrant build since April) and on-warrant stock up ~63 kt over three days, a more than 50% increase, which broke the squeeze and collapsed the cash-3M spread. Delivery-pressure verdict therefore reads 'stressed, relieving'. Same unvintaged-secondary limitation applies.
